### 10.3 Known identifier inconsistencies (recorded, not corrected)

These are defects in the accepted corpus. 09C records them so engineering does not guess; it does not edit B-09, the formula register or the AX contracts.

1. **`ALF-07` has two meanings.** `ALL-085` assigns it to `ALLIANCE_ROSTER_FULL`; `F-AL-005` assigns it to `SELF_APPROVAL_PROHIBITED`. Both are candidate-only contexts. Engineering must not emit `ALF-07` without a disambiguating message until the owner or a later prompt resolves it.
2. **Discord URL validation has three references.** `ALL-166` says `ALF-04`; `AX-19` says `ALF-11`; `AX-03` reserves `ALF-04` for `INVALID_DISCORD_URL`. The link is unapproved under `UD-048`, so no runtime path exists today.
3. **`ALF-25` is broader in use than its definition.** The definition speaks of incomplete approval/consent/scope; `ALL-197` also uses it for an unknown or unregistered treaty type/effect. 09C uses `ALF-25` for both and documents the stretch rather than inventing a new code.
4. **`ALF-13`–`ALF-20` are reserved but undefined.** The rulebook declares the `ALF-01`–`ALF-29` space but only defines or names the codes above. No workflow may invent meanings for the gap.

## 11. Concurrency and multiplayer-integrity matrix

Alliance state is shared by many players and by turn-boundary settlement. The following guarantees are binding for engineering; they describe behaviour the specification requires, not verified runtime behaviour.

| # | Concurrent situation | Required guarantee | Mechanism the spec relies on | Test |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Two officers edit the same bracket before the freeze | Last committed version wins by version order; no merged partial rates | Versioned bracket object; one active version per Alliance | `AAT-036` |
| 2 | Bracket edit races the turn freeze | Either fully before (applies) or fully after (next turn); never half-applied | One immutable snapshot taken at freeze | `AAT-051` |
| 3 | Two officers assign the same member to different brackets | Exactly one active assignment per member per Alliance; the later committed assignment supersedes | Per-Assignment uniqueness constraint | `AAT-040` |
| 4 | Member leaves while a tax settlement is running | Membership is read from the frozen snapshot; leave applies to the next boundary | Frozen roster | `AAT-045` |
| 5 | Applicant accepted twice from two sessions | One membership record; second acceptance is a no-op or rejection | Atomic transition from `PENDING` | `AAT-009` |
| 6 | Two applications for the last candidate roster slot | No cap exists today; if a cap is ever approved, one acceptance succeeds and the other is rejected atomically | No approved cap; candidate guard only | `AAT-010` |
| 7 | Two donations confirmed from the same dialog | Distinct idempotency keys or one replay returning the original receipt; never two debits for one confirmation | Idempotency key per confirmation | `AAT-058` |
| 8 | Two operational authorisations compete for the same `AVAILABLE` value | At most one reserves the amount; the second gets `ALF-28` | Reservation against `AVAILABLE` | `AAT-067` |
| 9 | Settlement retried while the first attempt is still committing | At most one settlement; the retry returns the original receipt or waits | Atomic transaction + idempotency | `AAT-066` |
| 10 | Treaty activation races an attack submission | Whichever boundary commits first governs; execution revalidates current records | Revalidation at execution | `AAT-091` |
| 11 | Member joins a party Alliance after attack submission | Execution check sees current membership and blocks if a shared Alliance now exists | Current records, not cached roster | `AAT-098` |
| 12 | NAP amendment races an attack | Execution uses the coverage set effective at the execution boundary | Versioned coverage set | `AAT-093` |
| 13 | Two Alliances found with the same tag simultaneously | Exactly one succeeds; the other gets `ALF-01` | Uniqueness constraint | `AAT-002` |
| 14 | Dissolution races a donation | A donation against a `DISSOLVED` Alliance fails atomically; no value is stranded | State check + atomic transfer | `AAT-109` |
| 15 | Dissolution races a member leave | Both end in `FORMER_MEMBER`; no double removal event | Idempotent membership transition | `AAT-017` |
| 16 | Permission revoked while an authorised action is in flight | Execution-time check fails; the action is rejected, not completed | Revalidation at execution | `AAT-032` |
| 17 | Two members record competing contact or succession claims | Each claim is stored as separate evidence; no contact-pointer change is executable; no office is created or transferred | Append-only evidence; contact record unchanged | `AAT-033`, `AAT-111` |
| 18 | ARL reconciliation runs during settlement | Reads a consistent snapshot; a discrepancy is disclosed, never netted | Append-only events + reconciliation | `AAT-071` |
| 19 | Two audit writers append simultaneously | Both events survive in order; no overwrite | Append-only audit spine | `AAT-095` |
| 20 | Two nations consent to the same treaty version at once | Both consents recorded independently; coverage set complete only when all required consents exist | Per-nation consent records | `AAT-077` |

| # | Threat | Attack path | Primary control(s) | Rule | Test | Residual / owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Rogue officer drains treasury | Attempts a general withdrawal | No general withdrawal exists; audit backstop | `ALL-101`, `UD-046` | `AAT-062` | Withdrawal policy open |
| 2 | Privilege escalation via role creation | Grants permissions beyond own set | Anti-escalation subset check | `ALL-062` | `AAT-030` | None |
| 3 | Hostile leadership takeover | Uses a vacancy to seize control | No executable process; no automatic succession; owner policy open | `ALL-056`, `UD-043` | `AAT-034` | Succession policy open |

| 7 | Sybil alliance proliferation | Founds many Alliances | Naming uniqueness + audit; fee candidate only | `ALL-013`, `ALL-014` | `AAT-002` | `UD-040` open |
| 8 | Predatory lending / debt slavery | Engine-enforced debt | No engine loans or garnishment | `ALL-118`, `ALL-120` | `AAT-110` | `UD-046` open |
| 9 | Extortion via asset lockup | Blocks exit until payment | Unblockable leave | `ALL-091` | `AAT-014` | None |
| 10 | Bypassing embargoes via alliance | Routes transfers through an Alliance | Same screening as national transfer | `ALL-159`, `AX-17` | `AAT-069` | None |
| 11 | Weaponised domestic instability | Uses alliance tools to alter approval | Zero domestic impact | `ALL-158`, `AX-13` | `AAT-105` | None |
| 12 | Coercive military deployment | Alliance commits member troops | National command sovereignty; no war drag | `ALL-136`, `ALL-141` | `AAT-110` | Prompt 10 |
| 13 | Discord impersonation / phishing | Malicious invite URL or bot | No API; URL validation unapproved | `ALL-165`–`ALL-168` | `AAT-110` | `UD-048` open |

| 15 | Orphaned Alliance on abandonment | Leader vanishes | Constitution-based contingency; audit | `ALL-054`, `ALL-057` | `AAT-034` | `UD-043` open |
| 16 | Bypassing Global Trade gates | Alliance market channel | No alliance market channel | `ALL-009`, `AX-26` | `AAT-110` | `D-122` preserved |
| 17 | Retroactive law enforcement | Applies amendment backwards | Non-retroactive amendments and snapshot | `ALL-028`, `ALL-184` | `AAT-026` | None |
| 18 | Concealment of administrative abuse | Suppresses audit | Append-only immutable audit | `ALL-154`, `AX-21` | `AAT-101` | None |
| 19 | Covert taxation / silent deduction | Taxes stockpiles or hides a rate | Base, snapshot, permission, statement, audit | `ALL-179`–`ALL-186` | `AAT-048` | None |
| 20 | Forged or double-settled donation | Replays confirmation | Authentication, idempotency, receipt | `ALL-190`–`ALL-193` | `AAT-058` | None |

## 14. Acceptance-test matrix (`AAT-001`–`AAT-132`)

These are specification acceptance tests. They are executed later against an implementation; none has been executed here. A test passes only when every expected condition holds, every prohibited outcome is absent, and the named audit/receipt exists. The tables in §14.1–§14.7 are the behavioural index; §14.8 indexes the document-level traceability and evidence checks; §14.9 gives the full 26-field execution record for every test.

## 15. Exhaustive bidirectional traceability

### 15.1 Method

The authority order is `16_alliances.md` (rule text) → `16_alliances_formula_register.md` (arithmetic) → `16_alliances_integration_contracts.md` (cross-system behaviour) → `03_requirements_traceability.md` (wording and status) → decision registers → this companion (workflows, edges, tests, handoff). This companion adds no rule and changes no accepted identifier.

Rules are listed as inclusive ranges. Expansion rule: a row `ALL-a`–`ALL-b` covers every integer identifier from `a` to `b`; ranges never overlap and together cover `ALL-001`–`ALL-226`. Requirement ranges likewise cover every integer from `REQ-534` to `REQ-653` exactly once. Individual workflow-to-rule and workflow-to-test rows remain authoritative in §5 field 18.

### 15.12 Downstream subsystem dependencies (corrected ownership)

The B-section titles below are the official titles in [`02_master_game_design_bible_outline.md`](02_master_game_design_bible_outline.md). A dependency is not a transfer of ownership: B-09 remains the Alliance rule source, and the named section owns only its own subject.

| B section (official title) | Dependency on this companion | What must not be inferred | Verification owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| **B-03 — Accounts, nation creation and progression** | Supplies account and nation onboarding, one-player-one-nation identity and the shared-network/restricted-pair controls that the attack validator reads (`AX-01`, `AX-02`) | That B-03 is diplomacy, or that an Alliance can override a shared-network restriction | Prompt 03 (authoritative); Prompt 10 consumes the restricted-pair layer |
| **B-08 — Diplomacy** | Owns national diplomatic state, national treaties and the national sovereignty boundary; supplies the national treaty/NAP layer (`AX-15`, `AX-29`) | That an Alliance treaty overrides a national treaty or embargo; that an Alliance office may sign or consent for a nation | Prompt 08 (authoritative); Prompt 10 consumes the national-treaty layer |
| **B-09 — Alliances and alliance management** | Owns Alliance membership, governance, taxation, donations, ARL, Alliance treaties/NAP and the workflows in this companion | That this companion creates a new rule or authorizes implementation | Prompt 09 (authoritative); Prompts 10–15 consume only |
| **B-10 — Warfare, campaigns and postwar settlements** | Owns actual attack, campaign and settlement execution; must call the B-09 validator at submission and execution (`AX-18`, `AX-30`) | That blocked attacks consume readiness/OP/damage; that a new attack type bypasses the validator; that B-09 owns war execution | Prompt 10 |
| **B-12 — Fair play, player protection, privacy and administration** | Owns audit ingestion, fair play, player protection, privacy, reporting, moderation and administrative safeguards; receives `AUD-AL-001`–`019` and enforces field visibility (`AX-10`, `AX-21`, `AX-23`) | That optional settings suppress `AUD-AL-017`; that platform moderation is Alliance expulsion or creates an Alliance appeal right | Prompt 12 |
| **B-13 — Interface and player journeys** | Owns player-visible presentation and delivers `AN-01`–`AN-16` as structured records; consumes §8 journeys and the screens in §16.3 | Any authoring, reply, voice or real-time channel; any new rule, default rate or withdrawal button | Prompt 13 |
| **B-14 — Formulas, numerical rules and balance** | Owns numerical formulas, mathematical behaviour, balance and calibration; consumes `F-AL-006`/`F-AL-008` and the worked-example obligations | Any moderation or privacy ownership; any invented capacity, default rate, fee or dual approval | Prompt 14 |
| **B-15 — Cross-system interactions (Bible assembly: `22_master_game_design_bible.md`)** | Assembles the accepted authoritative specifications and companions, including this one, without duplicating or changing their rules | A competing Alliance rule set, a renumbered identifier or a claim of implementation | Prompt 15 |
| Economy (`B-04`/`B-02`) | Provides canonical transfers and production events used by tax/donation | Any minting, stockpile access or alternate ledger | Prompt 14 / implementation stage |
| Global Trade (`B-07`) | `D-122`/`REQ-513`/`G-1`–`G-6` remain authoritative; no alliance market channel | Any trade bypass or tariff | Prompt 14 / release gate |

**Explicit correction.** Earlier wording in this section labelled **B-03 as diplomacy**, **B-12 as audit only**, **B-13 as notifications only** and **B-14 as moderation**. Those labels were wrong. The current table uses the official outline: **B-03 is accounts/nation creation/progression**, **B-08 owns diplomacy**, **B-12 owns fair play, protection, privacy, reporting, moderation and administration**, **B-13 owns interface and player journeys**, **B-14 owns formulas and balance**, and **B-15 assembles the Bible**. Moderation is **not** a B-14 responsibility.

### 15.14 Classified forward register (every source identifier)

**Classification vocabulary.** `DIRECT` — the mapped workflow executes the named behaviour, or directly implements its refusal/record-only boundary, and the named test asserts it. `SUPPORTING` — the identifier constrains or supplies evidence for the mapped workflow but does not itself execute the named behaviour. `DEFERRED` — the behaviour belongs to another prompt or to an Open owner decision; no executable workflow exists and a downstream owner is named. `NOT APPLICABLE` — the identifier is withdrawn, reserved-undefined or otherwise outside the workflow's scope. `NOT APPLICABLE` is never used to hide a missing mapping.

**Authorisation vocabulary.** `approved` — an accepted rule or owner-authorized capability. `narrowly authorized` — executable only inside the exact `D-140`/`D-141` scope named by the row. `provisional` — specified as candidate or provisional design, not an approved release rule. `blocked` — the mapped workflow implements only the refusal or record-only boundary; the underlying policy remains Owner-reserved. The companion never promotes a `blocked` row to approval.

**Evidence status.** Every row is `SPECIFICATION-DEFINED`: the specification defines the mapping. No row is `DOCUMENT-VALIDATED` until the validator in §19.3 runs, and no row has implementation or runtime evidence. Implementation and runtime statuses are stated once in §19.3–§19.4.

**Classification discipline.** `DIRECT` is not used to imply approval: 10 owner-reserved `UD` rows and the blocked succession, permission, treasury, appeal and Discord rows carry `blocked` in the authorisation column. `SUPPORTING` is used where a rule constrains rather than executes. `DEFERRED` names a downstream owner. `NOT APPLICABLE` is limited to withdrawn or reserved-undefined identifiers. No accepted rule is reclassified as approved by this table.

## 16. Cross-prompt handoffs

Each handoff states what the downstream prompt must consume, what it must not reinterpret, and the evidence it must produce. None of these prompts is started by 09C.

### 16.1 Prompt 10 — Warfare, campaigns and postwar settlements

**Consume.**

- `AX-18` and `AX-30`: one canonical server-side validator, called at submission and again at execution/settlement, on every attack path.
- Four cumulative layers, in this order: B-03 restricted pairs, B-08 national treaty/NAP, B-09 same-Alliance ban (`ALL-209`–`ALL-212`), B-09 `AT-T01` covered-set NAP (`ALL-206`–`ALL-208`).
- Block semantics: fail-closed, no crowns/resources/readiness/OP/damage consumed, plain-language reason, mandatory `AUD-AL-017`, no confiscation or retaliation.
- Coverage inputs: current membership records and the treaty's recorded consenting set, not a cached roster or an alliance-wide assumption.
- Boundary rules: membership changes, NAP activation/amendment/expiry and campaign state take effect at the boundary defined in `ALL-211` and §7.5.

**Do not reinterpret.**

- Do not add an Alliance coverage rule, a consent rule, a delegation, or a waiver.
- Do not let a new attack type, interface, campaign path or administrative override skip the validator.
- Do not resolve `UD-044` or `UD-047`.
- Do not treat a record-only `AT-E00` treaty as a NAP.

**Evidence Prompt 10 must produce.** A path inventory proving every attack entry point calls the validator; negative tests for each layer; execution-time change tests; audit samples for every block; a statement of where the validator sits in the damage pipeline.

### 16.2 Prompt 12 — Fair play, player protection, privacy and administration

**Consume.**

- Field visibility and applicant privacy (`ALL-086`, `ALL-156`, `REQ-057`, `AX-10`).
- Confidentiality of tax reports, receipts and member contribution history; who may read them (`ALL-186`, `ALL-225`, `REQ-653`).
- Retention and access rules for treaty-consent records (`AUD-AL-016`).
- Authorization model at execution time (`ALL-071`, `REQ-553`) and privileged-read auditing.
- The strict boundary: platform moderation is not Alliance expulsion; no Alliance appeal right exists (`ALL-158`, `UD-044`).
- Operator correction under `DPE-049` and privileged-read auditing under `DPE-054` from the B-08 companion.

**Do not reinterpret.**

- Do not create an Alliance appeal, hearing, redress or reconsideration path.
- Do not decide who may expel a member.
- Do not leak tax or contribution data through moderation tooling.
- Do not resolve `UD-044`.

**Evidence Prompt 12 must produce.** A field-by-field access matrix for tax/contribution/treaty data; moderation-tooling data-flow review; appeal-boundary text reviewed against `UD-044`; privileged-read audit samples.

### 16.3 Prompt 13 — Interface, screens and player journeys

**Consume.**

- The 22 journeys in §8 and the 16 notification labels in §12.
- Screens required: tax bracket creation/management with separate Crowns and resource percentages; member assignment; effective turn and policy version before confirmation; tax history and receipts; aggregate contribution reports; donation confirmation and receipt; the four ARL categories; unavailable operational purposes and their failure states; treaty offer/consent/coverage; blocked-attack explanation; permission-denied states.
- Every screen must state which B-09 section governs it.
- No native real-time chat, voice or third-party messaging integration; structured notifications and audit visibility only.

**Do not reinterpret.**

- Do not add a rule, a default rate, a fee or a capacity value.
- Do not design a withdrawal button or an "upkeep" action that implies an approved cost schedule.
- Do not show a NAP as covering the whole roster.
- Do not make Discord or a second account necessary for any step.

**Evidence Prompt 13 must produce.** A screen-to-rule map; journey walkthroughs for J1–J22; empty/error/unavailable states; copy that distinguishes `AT-E00` from `AT-E01`, covered from non-covered, and available from reserved ARL value.

### 16.4 Prompt 14 — Numbers, formulas, balance and worked examples

**Consume.**

- `F-AL-006` tax arithmetic exactly: cumulative gross, cumulative due with floor, event delta, per-turn tax, net; no independent per-event floor, no floating point.
- `F-AL-008` ARL arithmetic and the invariant `AVAILABLE = RECEIVED − RESERVED − EXPENDED`.
- Per-Alliance assignment and the reversible 0% attribution safeguard (`UD-040` preserved).
- 100% Crowns tax and maintenance interaction; resource production-chain accounting after tax.
- Candidate parameters remain labelled: `F-AL-001`–`F-AL-005`, `F-AL-007`.
- No cost schedule exists; operational funding `Valid(q) = 0` today.

**Do not reinterpret.**

- Do not lower the 0–10,000 bp ceiling or invent a default rate.
- Do not invent capacity, storage, fee or dual-approval values.
- Do not resolve `UD-040` or `UD-046`.
- Do not present a candidate baseline as a release rule.

**Evidence Prompt 14 must produce.** Hand-computable worked examples for multi-event, multi-asset, 0%, 100%, multi-Alliance and 0%-fallback cases; a numerical conformance checklist against `F-AL-006`/`F-AL-008`; explicit dependency notes for every Open value.

### 16.5 Prompt 15 — Assemble and verify the Master Game Design Bible

**Consume.**

- This companion as the canonical Alliance workflow and acceptance reference; `16_alliances.md` remains the rule authority.
- §15 as the traceability spine; §17 as the evidence ledger; §19 as the 09C acceptance record.
- The known gaps in §10.3 and §15.13 must be carried into the Bible's open-issues register, not silently "fixed".

**Do not reinterpret.**

- Do not renumber `ALL`, `REQ`, `AX`, `F-AL`, `AUD-AL`, `AT`, `AOP`, `ALF`, `D`, `DD` or `UD` identifiers.
- Do not mark Stage 2 complete on the basis of 09C; 09C is one system's workflow specification.
- Do not claim implementation, runtime testing, live balance or release readiness.

**Evidence Prompt 15 must produce.** A Bible entry point that links rulebook, formula register, contracts, requirements and this companion; a final orphan report; a consolidated unresolved-decision register; a statement of what remains unverified.

### 17.3 Evidence rules

A gate passes only when its evidence exists, is recorded and is reviewed. A design document, a planned test, a roadmap entry or a developer assurance is not evidence. 09C itself supplies **specification evidence only**: complete workflows, edge cases, failure contracts, concurrency guarantees, notifications, threat controls, tests and traceability. It does not supply implementation evidence and must not be described as doing so.

## 18. Implementation handoff

This section is a build-order guide, not code. It defines what engineering must preserve when implementation is authorised; it authorises nothing.

### 18.1 Required conceptual objects

| Object | Minimum fields | Invariants |
|---|---|---|
| Alliance | ID, name, tag, status, founding turn, contact | Unique normalised name/tag; one contact; `ACTIVE`/`DISSOLVED` |
| Membership | Nation, Alliance, state, join/leave turn, reason | One row per nation per Alliance; exactly one of three states |
| Application | Nation, Alliance, turn, text, state | One live application per nation; atomic decision |
| Position / permission grant (candidate object; structured creation, assignment or deletion blocked under `UD-045`) | Position, precedence, capability set, holder | No wildcard; subset of grantor's capabilities at grant time; execution-time recheck |
| Constitution version (candidate object; creation, publication and activation blocked under `UD-045`) | Version, hash, text, effective turn | Immutable published versions; non-retroactive |
| Tax bracket / assignment | Alliance, version, per-asset bp, member | 0–10,000 integer bp; one active assignment per member per Alliance; 0% fallback |
| Tax assessment / receipt | Nation, turn, snapshot, cumulative gross/due, event tax, net | `F-AL-006`; once-only; no stockpile base |
| Donation | Donor, Alliance, asset, amount, key, receipt | Atomic matched transfer; idempotent |
| ARL ledger | Alliance, asset, category events | `AVAILABLE = RECEIVED − RESERVED − EXPENDED`; append-only |
| Operational authorization | Purpose, schedule, asset, amount, sink, actor, key, status | Closed registry; exact schedule match; platform sink only |
| Treaty object | ID, type, effect, parties, approvals, consents, covered set, term, status | Two active Alliances; structured effect only; per-version consent |
| Attack validation decision | Attacker, defender, layers, decision, boundary | Called at submission and execution; fail-closed; `AUD-AL-017` on block |
| Notification record | Event, audience, dedup key | Structured only; no chat |

### 18.2 Build order

1. Identity, Alliance, membership, application and lifecycle (`ALW-001`–`ALW-007`).
2. Descriptive constitution and position authoring plus the refusal path for structured management (`ALW-008`–`ALW-012`). Structured constitution, position, role and permission management is blocked under `UD-045` and must not be built as executable; only the narrow tax-management set is executable.
3. Tax bracket, assignment, snapshot and settlement (`ALW-014`–`ALW-020`) with `F-AL-006` conformance tests.
4. Donations and ARL accounting (`ALW-021`–`ALW-023`) with conservation tests.
5. Operational funding **interface and refusal path only** (`ALW-024`–`ALW-026`); no schedule exists.
6. Treaty and NAP lifecycle (`ALW-027`–`ALW-037`) with per-version consent.
7. Shared attack validator (`ALW-038`–`ALW-040`) exposed to Prompt 10.
8. Audit, privacy and notification surfaces (`ALW-041`–`ALW-044`).
9. Failure, retry and ambiguity paths (`ALW-045`–`ALW-049`).

### 18.3 Do-not-build list

Do not build, stub, feature-flag or "beta-enable": a general treasury withdrawal; a player distribution, grant, loan, aid, refund, dividend or salary; a second approver or treasury office; a native ballot; an announcement board; real-time chat; a Discord bot/API/OAuth/webhook/account link; an automatic successor/steward; an Alliance appeal; a market channel; an Alliance-owned military; any automatic war entry.

### 18.4 Engineering acceptance

Engineering must reproduce `AAT-001`–`AAT-132`, including every negative test, before claiming the Alliance system works. Until then the correct status is: **"Alliance rules accepted; workflows and tests specified; implementation not started; no runtime evidence."**

### 19.2 Mandatory high-risk negative-test index

The following negatives are mandatory. They are specified in §14; the index exists so a later reviewer cannot claim coverage from a happy-path test.

|---|---|---|

| An Alliance office consents for a nation | `AAT-077` | Rejected; consent is the owner's alone |
| Silence is treated as consent | `AAT-078` | Consent set incomplete; nation uncovered |
| A non-covered member is treated as a non-member | `AAT-079` | Remains a full member; only coverage differs |
| A new member inherits coverage | `AAT-080` | No coverage without fresh consent |
| A record-only treaty executes a mechanic | `AAT-074` | `AT-E00` executes nothing |
| Free treaty text creates mechanics | `AAT-075` | No NLP execution |

| A non-covered nation is blocked by a NAP | `AAT-092` | Not blocked by the NAP |
| An attack path bypasses the validator | `AAT-093` | Same validator runs at every entry point |

| The snapshot is not deterministic | `AAT-051` | One immutable snapshot |
| Ambiguous attribution is guessed | `AAT-050` | 0% fallback and recorded reason |
| A 100% rate creates debt | `AAT-049`, `AAT-055` | Net zero; no negative balance |

| Invalid tax permissions succeed | `AAT-042` | Rejected with `ALF-21` |
